answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vesting: every agent earns rewards into a locked pool released across many epochs, so identity value grows with age. At a summit of network operators, agents stake reputation like a prism splitting each payout into slices only claimable later; a pearl of long-lived accounts compounds, while flash-farm sybils forfeit unvested earnings on exit. Attacking thus costs capital locked for months per fake identity, making bulk identity creation unprofitable.
